status: draft — pre-build naming contract, not yet implemented
philosophy: Minor adjusts for major results. Nothing named here is invented beyond what the brainstorm already decided — every gap that had to be filled to make the naming complete is flagged "inferred": true with a reason. Where the brainstorm proposed two options for the same thing, "resolution_notes" records which one wins and why.
external_system: WAHA (WhatsApp HTTP API), self-hosted, engine GOWS

resolution_notes.conflict: HMAC secret storage — global env WHATSAPP_HOOK_HMAC_KEY vs per-session key set in the Apollo plugin
resolution_notes.resolved: per-session, stored as the WP option apollo_wa_hmac_key, non-autoload
resolution_notes.why: brainstorm explicitly states 'preferir por session no Apollo'; per-session also lets the key rotate without touching the WAHA container env and without a restart

resolution_notes.conflict: Queue status naming — 'blocked' (screen-3 table) vs 'blocked_privacy' (later UX status line)
resolution_notes.resolved: blocked_privacy is canonical; 'blocked' is not used anywhere in code
resolution_notes.why: the plugin will likely grow other non-privacy block reasons (rate limit, WAHA send failure) later — a bare 'blocked' would collide with those; 'blocked_privacy' names the reason, not just the state

resolution_notes.conflict: Approve button copy — 'Aprovar' (control label in the table) vs 'Processar entrada' (the line that says the button must not promise success)
resolution_notes.resolved: internal action key stays approve; the rendered button label is 'Processar entrada'. 'Recusar' keeps its literal label — no ambiguity was raised for it
resolution_notes.why: explicit in the brainstorm: the button can't promise 'entrou' before the async add/invite chain resolves

resolution_notes.conflict: Engine — GOWS vs NOWEB vs Baileys(WEBJS) for the daemon session
resolution_notes.resolved: GOWS (whatsmeow/Go) is the only engine used in production; NOWEB is explicitly avoided ('Invalid patch mac' corruption pattern), Baileys/WEBJS is lab-only if WAHA itself ever needs replacing
resolution_notes.why: stated directly and repeatedly — GOWS has native LID resolution, the keepalive envs, and is what the WAHA container defaults to for long-lived sessions

resolution_notes.conflict: keepalive — write a custom daemon (whatsapp-keeper style) vs use the engine's built-in setting
resolution_notes.resolved: WAHA_GOWS_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_MIN/MAX env vars only, no companion process
resolution_notes.why: explicit veto: 'whatsapp-keeper não é o melhor repo pra você... o keepalive já veio no motor'

resolution_notes.conflict: check-exists endpoint shape — with vs without {session} in the path
resolution_notes.resolved: GET /api/contacts/check-exists?session={session}&phone={phone} — session is a query param, not a path segment
resolution_notes.why: verified against WAHA's ContactsController — check-exists lives under /api/contacts with session in the query string; this differs from the newer /api/{session}/groups/... family used elsewhere. _inferred: true — confirm both shapes against the exact 2026.8.2 swagger before writing the HTTP client, WAHA has mixed legacy/session-prefixed routes across controllers.

resolution_notes.conflict: capability for admin actions — brainstorm says 'cap manage_options / cap Apollo' without picking one
resolution_notes.resolved: custom capability manage_apollo_whatsapp, mapped to manage_options by default on activation
resolution_notes.why: inferred — no Apollo-suite-wide capability convention was stated in this brainstorm; using a dedicated cap keeps this plugin consistent with WP best practice and lets a future Apollo-wide role map override the mapping without touching this plugin's code. Confirm against whatever capability convention the other ~40 apollo-* plugins already use, if any.

A_wordpress.role: apollo-core + apollo-whatsapp — login, users, events, admin UI. Never holds the WhatsApp session itself.
A_wordpress.runtime: PHP, LocalWP for lab / VPS for production
A_wordpress.fails_open_to: site keeps working if B is down; queue and pane just stop updating

B_waha.role: WAHA Docker container, session name apollo, engine GOWS
B_waha.network: bind 127.0.0.1 or a Docker network only — never public
B_waha.fails_open_to: if down, WhatsApp keeps running on the phone, but WordPress is blind to it

C_phone.role: operation phone — the device paired to the session
C_phone.constraint: must NOT be the Apollo verified Business number
C_phone.maintenance: open the WhatsApp app on it roughly once a week

capability.note: add_cap on activation, remove_cap on uninstall — never hardcode manage_options in the route/menu checks, always check the custom cap

webhook_inbound_headers.X-Webhook-Hmac-Algorithm: must equal literal string sha512, any other value is a 401
webhook_inbound_headers.X-Webhook-Timestamp: unix ms, used for the replay window

hmac_key.generated: wp_generate_password(48, true, true) on plugin activation
hmac_key.storage: WP option, non-autoload, never echoed to JS or the DOM, never committed to git
hmac_key.configured_on: the WAHA session's webhooks[].hmac.key — set via the WAHA API when the session is created/updated from screen 1

dedupe_transient.behavior_on_repeat: return 200 empty body — acknowledge without reprocessing, never 401 a legitimate retry twice

pipeline_order: 1. HTTPS only in production (LocalWP lab exempted)
2. read the raw body via file_get_contents('php://input') — never let WP parse JSON before the HMAC check
7. dedupe on X-Webhook-Request-Id via the apollo_wa_hook_{id} transient — seen before → 200 empty, do not reprocess
10. only then switch on payload.event — never eval, never raw SQL built from the body
security.rest_permission_callback: custom machine check (the pipeline above) — never is_user_logged_in, never __return_true with zero verification

outbound_auth.storage: WP option, non-autoload, plaintext only ever lives in WordPress — the WAHA container only stores its hash (WAHA_API_KEY=sha512:{hash})

not_security: ?token=... query string on the webhook URL — leaks into access logs, CDN logs, referrer headers
trusting payload.session alone without the HMAC — anyone can write that JSON
IP allowlist as the only control — Docker/NAT changes the source IP
=== instead of hash_equals for the HMAC compare
a REST route with __return_true and no signature check
logging the raw body next to the HMAC key — that logs the secret
checklist: HMAC key >= 32 bytes, generated on activate
SHA512 + hash_equals on the raw body
REST route has no cookie auth and fails closed
hmac/api keys never reach the front end
outbound calls to WAHA always send X-Api-Key
a 401 never reveals whether the key was 'close'

events_upcoming.owner: apollo-core (already exists — consumed, not owned, by this plugin's 'evento' keyword)

apollo_wa_waha_url.note: base URL of the WAHA container

apollo_wa_hmac_key.note: inbound webhook HMAC secret, see security.hmac_key

apollo_wa_group_approve_new_members.note: screen 1 card B toggle — turns on WhatsApp's own group join-approval

apollo_wa_rate_seconds.note: minimum seconds between outbound sends, anti-ban

_apollo_whatsapp_phone.note: the phone number the user entered/verified via OTP

_apollo_wa_candidates.note: both BR digit-count variants (12 and 13 digit) derived from _apollo_whatsapp_phone, see phone_resolution

_apollo_wa_jid.note: the JID that check-exists confirmed as real, cached so later sends skip re-resolving. Not explicitly named in the brainstorm but required by its own rule: 'confie no chatId que o check-exists devolveu', which has to be stored somewhere

queue.storage: apollo-core queue table/meta — no new custom post type for this

statuses.invited: 403 on add, invite link sent to the user's DM instead
statuses.pending_approval: join-request sitting in WhatsApp's own group approval queue
statuses.blocked_privacy: add failed (403) and the DM invite delivery also failed — genuine dead end, needs manual outreach. supersedes the earlier 'blocked' label, see resolution_notes
statuses.session_down: attempted while WAHA session was not WORKING

values.FLOW: reserved for a future multi-step flow — not used by the MVP keyword set
values.HUMAN: bot is muted for this user; admin is handling the thread manually

flow_state.human_timeout: 2 hours, or until admin clicks 'liberar' in the pane

keyword_map.evento | hoje | rolê: events.upcoming — GET /apollo/v1/events/upcoming, answered in the DM
keyword_map.humano | atendente: handoff — sets HUMAN + pings admin, badge in the pane
keyword_map.sair | para: idle — resets flow state to IDLE

flows_mvp.match_mode: exact or starts-with, never regex/fuzzy — a chatty bot in a group is the pattern the community flags as a ban risk
flows_mvp.fallback: one generic reply plus 'digita evento | entrar | humano'

reaction_to_wow.status: phase_2, not in the MVP webhook handler
reaction_to_wow.note: message.reaction webhook event is still subscribed at the session level, but no handler consumes it in v1

group.listens_only_to: the configured anchors (apollo_wa_group_anchors) or an explicit reply to the bot
group.on_anchor_hit: reply is sent to the user's DM (the 'whisper'), never back into the group
group.otherwise: mirrored into the pane only, no auto-reply
group.admin_send: composer default destination toggle, or the /grupo command override

dm.admin_send: composer default destination toggle, or the /dm {number} command override

2_session_strip.note: not a separate page — the live status strip rendered at the top of screen 1

7_user_inbox.location: "meus pedidos" block on the Apollo profile

L_waha_dashboard.audience: admin only, setup/debug — never linked to a regular user

commands./grupo: force send to the group regardless of the thread's default destination
commands./dm {number}: force send to a specific DM
commands./silent: record in WordPress only, do not send to WhatsApp
commands./humano: mark the current thread's flow_state as HUMAN

composer_commands.note: any admin-sent message carries fromMe on the WAHA side and must never re-trigger a keyword flow

pane.data_source: apollo-core's existing chat/notifications store — not the DOM, not a new CPT
pane.population: webhook events message / message.any write into the core store, the pane reads from it
pane.outbound: admin composer POSTs sendText to either the group JID or the open thread's JID
pane.mute_on_open: opening a thread in the pane mutes the bot for that thread (mirrors a human agent 'joining' without needing Chatwoot)

waha.dashboard_env: WAHA_DASHBOARD_ENABLED=false in production unless actively debugging

endpoints_used.check_exists: GET /api/contacts/check-exists?session={session}&phone={phone} — see resolution_notes on path shape
endpoints_used.put_contact: PUT /api/{session}/contacts/{chatId} — call 2-3x with a few seconds between calls, the device-side app can be flaky
endpoints_used.send_text: POST /api/sendText — session goes in the body, not the path (confirmed against WAHA's controller shape)

phone_resolution.br_rule: store both the 12-digit (pre-2012, no 9th digit) and 13-digit (post-ANATEL, with 9th digit) forms — never assume one is correct
resolution_order: use whichever candidate the endpoint reports exists=true
never trust raw user input for the add/send call — always use the check-exists result

steps: 1. session === WORKING? if not → status session_down, stop
8. Error 403 with AddRequest.Code in the body → send https://chat.whatsapp.com/{Code} to the user's DM → invited
9. Error 403 without a Code → GET invite-code, send that link instead → invited
10. invite DM delivery itself fails → blocked_privacy
add_chain.never_use_the_official_number_here: the Apollo verified Business number must never be paired into this WAHA session

cron.status: not built yet — this registry only reserves the naming
cron.trigger: WP-Cron with a lock, reuses the same composer/sendText path as the pane
cron.guard: only fires if GET /api/sessions/{session} reports WORKING
cron.rate: one send every 8-15s when flushing a queue, same anti-ban rationale as apollo_wa_rate_seconds

out_of_scope_v1: cloning the full WhatsApp Web UI in WordPress (media library, 400-chat inbox, statuses) — that stays on WAHA's own dashboard (screen L)
Chatwoot / Typebot / n8n — shelved until there are multiple human agents
auto-reply to every group message — anchor-only, whisper to DM
official WhatsApp Cloud API / Coexistence — revisit only if broadcast-at-scale or OTP templates become a requirement

glossary.JID: WhatsApp's internal chat identifier, e.g. 5521999990000@c.us for a DM or 120363...@g.us for a group
glossary.LID: the anonymized identifier WhatsApp is rolling out to replace phone-number-based identity inside groups by end of 2026
glossary.GOWS: the whatsmeow-based Go engine WAHA uses for the session — chosen over NOWEB and Baileys/WEBJS
glossary.whisper: a group-anchor keyword hit that gets answered in the user's DM instead of back into the group
